chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Manqari from his uncle who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever eats food to which he was not invited, he has only eaten a piece of the Fire.'

key_terms.لَمْ يُدْعَ إِلَيْهِ: to which he was not invited

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of eating food without being invited according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the spiritual gravity of *ghulul* (appropriation) in social dining, where accepting an uninvited meal is viewed as consuming a literal portion of Hellfire. It serves as a critical ethical guideline in Shia jurisprudence for maintaining modesty and respecting the host's generosity, linking physical consumption to spiritual purification.
